newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian Sugar-China crushing on, Thai premiums lower.
newsitem.headline: Asian Sugar-China crushing on, Thai premiums lower.

text.p: China's sugar crushing has started in some southern regions but Asian markets remained slack with Thai premiums easing on a lack of buyers, industry sources in China, Japan and Hong Kong said on Wednesday.

Some Chinese sugar factories this week had started buying new crop cane sugar for crushing in the southern province of Guangxi, China's main sugar producing area, and in the coastal province of Guangdong, sugar traders in Hong Kong said.
But Guangdong factories were paying about 330 yuan (US$40) per tonne of new crop cane, compared to 240-280 yuan ($30-34) paid by Guangxi crushers, said a senior sugar trader in Hong Kong.
"In Guangdong, if the factories don't pay those prices, no one will grow the cane," the trader said, noting that the province's farmers were not bound by government policy to grow cane.

In Guangxi, white sugar prices had dropped slightly further to 4,250 yuan ($512) per tonne this week, compared to 4,300-4,380 yuan ($518-527) per tonne last week, as more of the new crop entered the market, said a sugar factory manager by telephone from Guangxi.

China's sugar production in 1996 has officially been pegged at 6.6 million tonnes, but Hong Kong and China-based traders said their own estimates for this year's crop varied from 5.9 million to 6.2 million tonnes.
"The official forecast is always higher than the reality," said one sugar trader based in Hong Kong.
But planted acreages are dropping, and farmers are eyeing more lucrative crops, a China-based trader said.
Asian markets dragged, as Thai premiums slid and Indonesia was seen as the only active buyer of white sugar.

Sugar traders in the region said they remained bearish as China was not expected to enter the markets for another six months at least. Chinese sugar buying orders usually fuel bullish sentiment in the region.

Premiums for Thai raw sugar for January/March delivery eased to 0.70/0.90 cents (bid/offer) per pound over New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) FOB basis, down from 0.75/0.90 a week earlier, Tokyo traders said.
March/May and May/July deliveries were both quoted at 0.50/0.60 cents on the New York exchange, unchanged from a week earlier, they said.
"Premiums for the January/March period are easing gradually on a lack of buyers. The physical market in the Far East is still very quiet," a sugar trader at a major trade house said.
Once Indonesia stopped buying, white sugar prices would drop, said a Hong Kong-based trader.
White sugar to Indonesia was heard quoted at $320-330 per tonne, C&F Indonesia.
"Much of this is coming from India, which is going to export a lot," said another sugar trader with an international house.
The trader said he had heard Indonesia-bound sugar cargoes being loaded at India's eastern ports like Madras, but this could not be confirmed.
"There is something to the tune of 500,000 tonnes for shipment spread over October, November and December," the sugar trader said.
(US$1 = 8.3 yuan)
--Mishi Saran in Hong Kong (852) 2843 6358
--Eiichiro Tokumoto in Tokyo (813) 3432 7391
